title: WinUI refund amount preflight versus authoritative server clamp and ledger effects
scope: Bounded semantic comparison of active Cashier WinUI refund form/request construction against RefundOrderHandler, RefundRules, Order.ApplyRefund, refund API route, and refund integration-test source. The prior WPF/WinUI comparison covers uncertain request retry lifecycle; this comparison focuses on amount validation, authorization, remaining balance, and effects.
decision: The client rejects nonpositive amounts and values above its displayed remaining refundable balance, while the server independently clamps any requested amount to the remaining amount and rejects a resulting zero. This is a deliberate permissive server boundary rather than an over-refund path: order locking, aggregate invariants, protected source-account balance, transaction, immutable refund record and treasury movement constrain effects. Existing tests explicitly cover server clamp, same-key replay and concurrent distinct refunds without aggregate overdraw. No new divergence or finding was confirmed. Tests were read, not run.

behavior.client: OpenRefund initializes amount to total minus prior RefundAmount. SubmitRefundAsync rejects parse failure, amount <= 0 or amount greater than displayed remaining; it resolves orders_refund approval, creates a request, and retains the exact pending request on ambiguous outcome for same-ID retry during ViewModel lifetime.
behavior.server: RefundOrderHandler derives idempotency key, replays existing refund, authorizes orders_refund or manager approval, locks order, computes remaining and clamps requested amount. It rejects zero after clamp, verifies protected source-account balance, assigns operational shift policy, applies aggregate guard, appends refund+treasury movement+audit in one transaction, then commits.
behavior.domain: RefundableRemaining floors negative remainder at zero; ClampRefundAmount floors negative requested/remaining values at zero and caps above-remaining requests; Order.ApplyRefund rejects cancelled/multi orders, zero/negative amount or amount above remainder and sets Refunded only when fully exhausted.
behavior.tests: Source tests cover full/partial refunds, over-remaining clamp, same-key idempotent sequential replay, same-key concurrency, distinct-key same-order overdraw protection, authorization rejection and multi-payment rejection. These are source assertions only; no tests executed in this task.

counterevidence_and_limits: Client/server amount behavior differs intentionally in strictness: client provides preflight UX, server clamps rather than rejecting excessive positive requests; this remains bounded by actual remaining amount.
Tests are integration-test source using the project test host; they do not establish deployed SQL Server lock/transaction behavior in the live restaurant environment.
The prior WPF/WinUI retry comparison records WPF new-ID retries and WinUI in-memory pending request semantics; this artifact does not repeat its transport lifecycle findings.
No live endpoint, actual refund, user account, database or treasury operation was executed.
recommendation: Keep current client preflight and server-side clamp/aggregate/balance checks aligned with the documented refund contract. If owners prefer rejection rather than clamping, change server and client behavior together and update operator feedback; preserve non-over-refund, protected-source-account and idempotency invariants. Add/retain tests for exact remaining, over-remaining clamp/reject policy, zero/negative, authorization, insufficient account balance, same-key payload mismatch, process-loss recovery, and concurrent distinct-key attempts; execute database-backed tests against the supported SQL Server provider before any repair is accepted.
required_tests: UI request test rejects nonpositive and over-displayed-remaining values and sends selected amount/reason/approval fields.
Server tests establish expected clamp-versus-reject contract and verify a clamped amount is the amount in both OrderRefund and treasury movement.
No writes occur for zero/negative, missing authorization, multi-payment, or protected source-account insufficiency.
Same-key replay, payload mismatch, process restart and concurrent distinct-ID refunds preserve idempotency and total-refund limits under SQL Server.
runtime_status: NOT_EXECUTED; static source and test review only
limitations: Current source-level client and server behavior is bounded to amount and transaction semantics.
Concurrent refund test assertions were not executed and should not be treated as runtime verification.
CashierWinUI is the active source path in this comparison; legacy WPF deployment status remains unknown and its retry lifecycle is documented in the earlier comparison.
canonical_findings: No new finding; related existing refund/cash-custody and idempotency findings, if applicable, remain the canonical records.
